_note: Documentary spec for scripts/film.ts. Times are chapter-local seconds (u) or a narration paragraph (p) plus an offset (off), so they follow the voice. Camera: yaw -2.356 looks east from the French side, 0.785 looks west from the Austrian side, -0.785 looks north along the river from the south; tilt 0.61 is the game's default, higher looks down. sim = [from, to] in sim seconds.
end:
This film is a reconstruction.The positions and movements of individual units are illustrative. The order of battle follows the published accounts, and the places where those accounts disagree are marked on screen.
Sources: Wikipedia, World History Encyclopedia, historyofwar.org, napoleon-series.org, napoleon.org, jeanlannes.com (Bonaparte's report to the Directory, as printed in The Times, 24 May 1796), Warlord Games.

cards.text: THE BRIDGE OF LODI
Illustrative footage: French columns on the march
April 1796 · Montenotte, Millesimo, Dego, Mondovì
28 April · Armistice of Cherasco: Piedmont leaves the war
The feint at Valenza · the real crossing at Piacenza, some 80 km away
7 May · Dallemagne's advance guard crosses the Po
7–9 May · Fombio and Codogno · Laharpe is killed in the night fighting
10 May · Lodi, on the River Adda
Feldmarschall-Leutnant Karl Philipp Sebottendorf commands the rearguard. Beaulieu is not at Lodi.
Austrian rearguard: 6,577 men in the order of battle; 9,500 to about 12,000 in other accounts
First line: Carlstädter Grenz (2 bns) · Warasdiner Grenz · Nádasdy IR 39
Second line: Terzi IR 16 · Belgiojoso IR 44 · Thurn IR 43 · Archduke Joseph Hussars · Mészáros Uhlans
Austrian guns at the bridge: 12 to 14 in most accounts. Bonaparte's own report says 30.
The bridge: wooden, on piles, about 200 yards (180 m) long
Before 9 am · Dallemagne's advance guard reaches Lodi; Lannes's grenadiers clear the town
About nine hours pass before the bridge is attacked in earnest
About midday · Bonaparte arrives and brings the artillery up to the river
Beaumont's cavalry is sent upstream to find a ford
French guns: about 24 to 30. Austrian guns: 12 to 30. The accounts do not agree.
About 6 pm · The column forms in Lodi: the 2nd battalion of carabiniers, then the grenadiers
The head of the column seemed to hesitate; through a moment of hesitation perhaps all might have been lost.
cards.sub: Bonaparte's report to the Directory, as printed in The Times, 24 May 1796 (English translation)

cards.text: Berthier, Masséna, Cervoni, Dallemagne, Lannes and Dupas precipitated themselves at the head of a column, and decided the day.
cards.sub: Bonaparte's report, as printed in The Times (translation)

cards.text: One attack or two? Carabiniers first, or grenadiers? How far did the first wave get? The accounts differ.
Some men wade the shallows beside the bridge, firing up at the gunners
Sebottendorf counter-attacks; Masséna's and Augereau's men arrive
Beaumont's cavalry crosses by a ford: deep and slow, and the horse could not charge (Bonaparte's report)
The Austrians withdraw towards Crema and Cremona in the dusk
French losses: 'inconsiderable' (Bonaparte) · about 350 · about 1,000 · about 1,500. Austrian: 2,000 to 3,000 and 15 to 20 guns.
15 May · Bonaparte enters Milan
The battle of Lodi gives the Republic all of Italy.
